searchText: Heyo! Here is an Ethereum 2.0 Phase 1&2 Developer Experience Survey: https://hwwhww.typeform.com/to/McUlt8 We didn’t target at eth2 client devs in this survey because you all are familiar with it too well! 😄 But please help to share with other community members to gather more information! ❤️ Just finished it ✔️ **terencechain** Awesome. Thanks for putting that together! **shahankhatch** wrt BLS benchmarking, it looks like we're in the 20-40ms range as expected. Is there a link to the implementation that ran at 9ms on an i5? Is it related to the link shared above? https://ethresear.ch/t/fast-verification-of-multiple-bls-signatures/5407/10 **protolambda** The sigma prime bench runs sub 8 ms, ~5ms for my i7 2.6Ghz laptop even. (The 128 same message verify) That 128 verify doesn't use Vitalik's fast verification scheme It's only helpful when you have multiple signatures **shahankhatch** That's what I figured, but wasn't sure if there was some other secret sauce at play. **shahankhatch** Do you think it's because of Rust? Because the sigp code looks like it's aggregating pubkeys within the benchmark, which others don't do. **shahankhatch** So both aggregating plus verification is faster than anything.. **shahankhatch** I'm pretty new to rust, and when I try to run the sigp bench I'm being told 'can't find crate' for criterion. Help please? **shahankhatch** (apologies if this isn't the right chan for that kind of help, happy to move the convo) **jadler** <@455742294692200449> what version of rust and cargo are you using? I just checked out the sigp benches and I'm running them now seemingly without issue. **shahankhatch** 1.37.0? **jadler** (in reply to **shahankhatch**) Same. I have no idea then. **shahankhatch** Thanks for trying to help me @jadler **liangcc** did you build before benchmark? Try `cargo build --release` **shahankhatch** @liangcc I've tried that but get the same error. **shahankhatch** It builds successfully, but running `cargo bench` gives the error. You need to run with `cargo bench --features bench` 🙂 **shahankhatch** Of course it was at the end of the page! Aaand I didn't read that far! Damn, sorry folks **shahankhatch** Thanks very much Paul! **shahankhatch** all good now **shahankhatch** Looks like ~7ms on an i7 for aggregate-verify of 128 sigs

excerpts.author: hsiaowei
excerpts.content:
Heyo! Here is an Ethereum 2.0 Phase 1&2 Developer Experience Survey: https://hwwhww.typeform.com/to/McUlt8

We didn’t target at eth2 client devs in this survey because you all are familiar with it too well! 😄 But please help to share with other community members to gather more information! ❤️

excerpts.content: Just finished it ✔️

wrt BLS benchmarking, it looks like we're in the 20-40ms range as expected. Is there a link to the implementation that ran at 9ms on an i5?  Is it related to the link shared above? https://ethresear.ch/t/fast-verification-of-multiple-bls-signatures/5407/10

The sigma prime bench runs sub 8 ms, ~5ms for my i7 2.6Ghz laptop even. (The 128 same message verify)

excerpts.content: That 128 verify doesn't use Vitalik's fast verification scheme

excerpts.content: It's only helpful when you have multiple signatures
